questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function
questions.problem: Consider the function $f(x)={x}^{3}+{e}^{x}$ and the point $P(0,1)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(0,1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{3}+{e}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =3{x}^{2}+{e}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(0) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(0,1)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(1,0)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(0)} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Derivative Using Properties of Inverse Functions
questions.problem: Consider the function $f(x)={2}^{x}+1.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(5).$
questions.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(5),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(5)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(5))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(5).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(5)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(5) & =x \\ f(x) & =5 \\ {2}^{x}+1 & =5 \\ {2}^{x} & =4 \\ {2}^{x} & ={2}^{2} \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(5)=2.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={2}^{x}+1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{2} \\ {f}^{′}(2) & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(5) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(5))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function Using a Table
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse is

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Substituting $x=4,$ we have

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(4)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))}.
$$

From the table, we obtain ${f}^{-1}(4)=-3$ and ${f}^{′}(-3)=5.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Derivative Using Properties of Inverse Functions
questions.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(2),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(2)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(2))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(2).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(2)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(2) & =x \\ f(x) & =2 \\ {x}^{2}-x & =2 \\ {x}^{2}-x-2 & =0 \\ (x+1)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =-1,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of $y=f(x)$ is $x\le -1,$ we have ${f}^{-1}(2)=-1.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(-1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{2}-x \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2x-1 \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =2(-1)-1 \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(2) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(2))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-3)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
